subject.title: [Feature] Cron and subagent sessions lack user context for plugin OAuth tools

question: Should OpenClaw add a generic trusted requester-identity contract for cron and spawned subagent runs, and what identity, consent, audit, privacy, revocation, and concurrency boundaries must plugin OAuth tools obey?
rationale: This would expose user OAuth authority to unattended runtime paths, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent Plugin SDK/API shape or security posture.

options.title: Design Typed Requester Context
options.body: Add a narrow runtime and Plugin SDK seam for explicit requester identity after maintainers define consent, audit, privacy, revocation, concurrency, and multi-account behavior.

options.title: Keep Identity Plugin-Owned
options.body: Ask affected plugins to use plugin-owned scheduled-identity configuration while core avoids a generic unattended requester API for now.

options.title: Defer Pending Live Proof
options.body: Keep cron and spawned runs headless until maintainers have live evidence from more OAuth-dependent plugins and can size the product need.

recommendation.title: Design Typed Requester Context
recommendation.body: Add a narrow runtime and Plugin SDK seam for explicit requester identity after maintainers define consent, audit, privacy, revocation, concurrency, and multi-account behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined history across cron agent binding, sessions_spawn, and the plugin/runtime boundary touched by this API decision.
